reason: Q3 was solid and the outlook is constructive (low EU gas storage, fleet growth, strong gas carrier rates), but LNG spot rates are weak, the sell-side questions raised nothing new, and the +10.8% move already reflects most of it.
Q3 beat and a margin-driven operating income gain are offset by a Q4 revenue guide cut, quarter-to-date comps down and a pending promotional holiday, which the -5.2% move already largely reflects.

Record quarter and strong bookings are offset by a full-year guidance cut (top end lowered about $3M) due to pump ramp limits, with no disposables pull-through yet; the -7.4% move already looks like a fair reaction, so I see no clear unpriced edge.

Record EBITDA, early deleveraging and Nissens strength look solid, but full-year guidance was unchanged, the CFO is leaving (a former COO returns as interim), and TC inventory suggests softer pre-season orders, so the +19% move seems to have priced the beat.
Guidance raise (revenue up, opex down, cash roughly breakeven) and the Lilly deal are largely known or priced in; the -2.7% move is a modest reaction and the call adds little unreflected information.

Q3 beat guidance, record backlog, new $50M buyback (~10% of market cap) and in-line 2027 growth view, offset by FCF slip into next year, lower backlog conversion, raw-material headwinds and softer margins; the -2.2% move looks fair.

Q3 margin recovery and the near-breakeven adjusted loss look largely priced in by the +14.3% move; Q4 gross margin guided under pressure (more China mix, legacy contracts), net debt rose, and storage revenue recognition is delayed.
SHOP guidance raise and Ensign lease are largely expected and offset by a presentation-only FFO guidance cut, 8.2x leverage and concessions holding rate flat, so the -3% move looks fair.

Record revenue, backlog of $109M against a $150M guide the CEO called conservative, and a possible very large wafer-level burn-in decision in early 2026 point to modest upside drift, but the +18.6% move has priced in much of it.

Sales guide cut about 1.5 pts on weak volumes, but EBITDA and FCF guidance held and the 2027 outlook (8-12% growth, 10%+ growth at the key business) was positive; the +7.1% move already reflects this.

The stock fell 6.1% despite record bookings and backlog, a second guidance raise, and early 2027 color (Astrobotic $150-200M, core growth of at least 25%, EBITDA-positive exit by Q4 2027). Large EBITDA losses, low-double-digit gross margin, and binary Griffin-1 and CLPS 2.0 risks keep the score modest.

Beat-and-raise on sales with net leverage at 2.0x and a new $250M buyback starting in Q4 give modest support, but the +10% move already prices most of it, and gradual margin expansion, a lower Q4 EBITDA guide and a Q3 lift from India GST and a revenue-timing shift limit the upside.

Strong operating results and leasing, but the call confirms FFO growth is pushed out and higher rates trim next-year earnings; asset sales will dilute earnings. The -4.6% move already reflects most of this, so I see no clear edge.

Q3 margin and robotics beat (+71%) looks largely priced in after the +8.6% move; guidance was only reaffirmed and now assumes higher inflation that is not fully offset, plus weak cash flow, rising receivables and inventory, and soft APAC and Europe orders, so I see no clear unreflected edge.

Strong Q3 beat and raised-tone 2026 outlook (at least mid-single-digit growth) are largely priced in after +24%; Q4 guide implies decelerating growth (~8%) and EBITDA margin falls to ~17%, so the call offers no clear unpriced edge.

The -17.9% drop reflects a roughly $12M revenue guide cut driven by BGS weakness and PRP/PNS tracking a little shy of plan, while the reaffirmed EPS guide, early October BGS improvement, debt paydown and an ongoing takeover-driven strategic review roughly offset that, so I see no clear unpriced edge.

Small guide raise was offset by 4.7% organic growth, margin compression, an implied Q4 slowdown (4-6% revenue growth, ~21% EBITDA margin), 3-4 quarters of AWS migration drag, and acquisitions running below plan; the 6% drop seems to price most of this in.

Record quarter and a raised guidance floor were already known, and the -7.2% drop looks like the market pricing peak-earnings worries (Q4 EBITDA guided flat, P&A not expected to repeat, next-year view only 'a shot' at matching, free cash flow -$58.7M); the call has no clear unpriced information.

Strong call (20% procedure growth, Onyx alpha launch ahead of plan, new DRGs, imminent CMS office-payment ruling, lower opex guide) is mostly priced in after the +12% move, but guidance looks conservative (implied Q4 above 20%) and the catalysts could drive modest drift.

The stock fell 6.8% mainly on a seasonally softer Q4 (shipments down high single digits, about $10-15M shutdown hit, slightly lower mix), while the call also had a DLA award of up to $995M, a backlog into Q2, a $60/ton price increase and a buyback. That looks like a modest overreaction, but pricing in the annual contracts is still uncertain and DLA shipments start only in Q2.

Strong beat, home vertical +70%, new $50M buyback and a constructive soft-market outlook are real, but the Q4 guide implies revenue growth slowing to about 12% with VMM falling on agentic traffic investment, and the +23.8% jump already prices most of the relief.

The -15.6% drop already prices the main negatives (leverage of 1.3x vs the 1x target, LOE of $12.40/BOE, flat-to-modest 2027 production, flat capex). Management's cover is plausible but unproven (leverage back to 1x on a full quarter of DJ Basin, LOE easing, a protected dividend), so I see no clear unpriced edge.

Lymphedema grew 13% with Medicare recovery, EBITDA guide was raised and revenue guide held, but the airway clearance cut and tougher Q4 comparison offset that, and the +7.6% move already reflects most of it.

Record Q3 with a large margin step-up and management saying 9-month margins are sustainable, plus a net cash position and a new $100M credit line. The +22% move already prices most of it, and the higher tax rate, lumpy trading revenue, and landing gear backlog cut leave only modest further drift.

Beat, guidance raise, completed refinancings and deleveraging to about 6.4x are good news, but the +8.6% move has largely priced them in, and the implied Q4 same-store step-down and higher refinanced interest costs offset the positives.

Positive RedeS phase III topline and steady 10% revenue growth with guidance reaffirmed are offset by an FDA delay on the INT200 platelet PMA, a later CE mark timeline and international softness, so the +2.6% move looks roughly fair.

Full-year revenue and EBITDA guidance were cut on MCM delivery slippage, the CFO is retiring, and Q3 adjusted EBITDA was negative, which the 8% drop mostly reflects. The raised gross margin guidance and strong cash flow and debt paydown offset this, so I expect only a mild negative drift.

Record quarter and guidance raise were flattered by one-offs (low cats, reserve releases, LP returns) and management itself flagged a much lower normalized EPS baseline of $4.25-4.45; positives like the acquisitions and capital flexibility look largely priced in after the +5.1% move.

Solid Q3 (ADS +8.5%, op income +24%, special dividend) and Q4-to-date growth steady, but Q4 gross margin guided flat YoY with freight/fuel/tariff headwinds and a one-time tariff refund flattering Q3; the +8% move already prices the beat.

The Q3 miss was caused by European competition, and the Q4 EBITDA guide and margin investments were cut sharply, but the -18.6% move already prices this in. Business quality is intact (fleet +26%, strong LimePrime retention, positive free cash flow, $453M cash, no debt), and the competition may persist into next year, so I see no clear edge either way.

Q4 EBITDA guide cut ~$20M on timing slips (Gulf loop currents, Colombia) that management says are recoverable, with a raised 2026 FCF guide and preliminary mid-teens 2027 EBITDA growth that analysts read as mostly acquisition and deferral; the 12.7% drop already reflects the cut, so no clear leftover edge.

The call is a solid quarter (94.6% combined ratio, premium +13%, investment income +25%) but shows softening rate (+2% renewals), a slightly higher underlying loss ratio and a still-high expense ratio, and the 13.6% drop already prices most of that in, so I see no clear unreflected edge.

The +27.7% move already prices in the LS&H sale completion, ACV and IP inflection, and Q4 guide (recurring growth above 2%, margin above 45%); no clear unpriced information is left, and the drift after such a large jump is uncertain.

The +47% move already prices in the clear beat (revenue +11%, operating income +~50%), the $0.70 special dividend and the $50M buyback. Part of the margin gain was one-time (tariff refunds, inventory monetization, channel fill), management is cautious on Q4 consumer demand, and the call adds little the price has not absorbed.

Q4 utilization (mid-90s%), rates and terminal volumes are guided higher, leverage is down, buybacks are planned at a large discount to NAV, and the Hormuz-driven ton-mile tailwind continues. The +1.9% move reflects only part of this, and Q3 adjusted results were merely in line.

Q1 EBITDA of $31.3M is about 28% of the full-year guide midpoint and external cost per participant fell, while guidance was only reaffirmed with stated conservatism on rates and V28, so a raise looks likely; the +9.8% move already prices in much of this.

Government services margin guidance was cut and the supply-chain recovery slipped to end of Q1, but the EBITDA midpoint was affirmed and offshore energy strength plus buybacks offset it, so the 5.5% drop looks like a fair reflection.
Solid Q3 (ROE 16.9%, CR 85.7%) but management flags softening short-tail pricing, falling GWP, and book value down on mark-to-market; -2.3% move looks fair, nothing clearly unpriced.

Operationally strong quarter (record contribution margin, dividend up 12.8%, new buyback authorization, portfolio growth) but EBT fell to $19M from $43M and the +8.4% two-session move already reflects the beat. Little unpriced information remains.

The $80M+ savings program and the break-even FCF are offset by 4.5x leverage with a covenant waiver, China revenue down 45% and heading to 4-5% of sales, a one-time ~300bp Q3 gross margin boost, and a +2.3% move that already prices in the good news.

Clean beat with EBITDA growing faster than revenue, first Chicago licenses with go-live within weeks, and strong Fairmount results, but the +12.7% move already prices most of that in, and the Fairmount cost overrun and Las Vegas weakness are modest offsets.

Strong Q3 beat (sales +12.5%, Sand States +21%, EBITDA +18%), narrowed guidance and a $100M buyback were largely priced in by the +9.7% move; 2027 market guided flat and cost pass-through is a risk, so no clear residual edge.

Solid quarter (revenue +3%, gross profit +7%, $27M cash generated, debt down, AM&C +21%) but Print is shrinking, there was no Q&A and no guidance, and the call doesn't explain the -14.6% drop, so I see no clear unreflected edge.

Long-term EBITDA growth target raised to >15% with slower unit growth and FCF acceleration, plus an Investor Day next week as a catalyst, but traffic is negative and Q4 comp guidance is soft, and the +4.2% move already reflects much of this.

The 20% drop already reflects the FY guidance cut to the low end and the weak next-year guide (PTC roll-off, El Nino, higher interest), and the call adds nothing material beyond that, so I see no clear edge in either direction.

Strong Q3 (RevPAR +7.2%, September +11%), a second guidance raise, October RevPAR about +5.5% and an upbeat 2027 tone with acquisition appetite, but the price only moved +0.4%, so some of the momentum looks unpriced; the gain is limited by tougher World Cup comps and the CFO transition.
The -23.7% drop already reflects the negative adjusted EBITDA and energy-cost hit; the $100M cost program and trade-protection gains offset a weak Q4 outlook, so I see no clear unpriced edge.

Solid beat-and-raise (25% growth, US +41%, NDR 118%, guide to upper end despite FX, 95% of next-year growth already signed, EBITDA loss narrowing) and the stock was down 2%, so there is modest unreflected upside. The FX headwind and planned 2027 investments limit the score.

BDC Q3 had NII covering the dividend, NAV stable, and a new JV; the 7% jump already reflects these, and there are offsetting signs (watch list up, GAAP realized losses, NII down quarter-on-quarter), so no clear unpriced edge.

Q3 beat on margins, helped by one-time duty and pricing gains, but Q4 guide is softer (lower daily volumes, specialty and structural margins stepping down, $15-20M inventory build, falling housing starts), so the 5.4% drop looks mostly fair and I see no clear mispricing.

Flat FFO of $0.35, a 99.3% occupied portfolio, 100% rent collection and a covered $0.30 dividend are offset by a stalled acquisition pipeline, about $100M of debt to refinance at higher rates, and the Austin office losing GM; the 6% drop already reflects most of this.

Strong beat and guidance raise are real, but the +18% move already prices them in. Offsetting: ~$5M high-margin pull-forward, a soft implied H2 after Q2 was called the low point, leverage near 4x, and negative FCF so far.

Call was in-line with prior guidance (cash >$70M, guidance maintained, nothing new on FDA review); the key binary catalyst is the Anaphylm FDA decision about 88 trading days out, which is beyond the 20-day window, and the +0.8% move reflects little new information.

Strong HPC quarter, a MBO interest disclosure and a live sale review are offset by the review slipping to Q1, Temiscaming carrying costs of $2-3M per month, and a 7.2% pop that already prices much of this in.

Lower 2026 cash burn guidance, MOBIUS commissioning on track and a Korea JV still unsigned look largely priced in after the +14.2% move; no customer supply deals secured and requalification is pending.

Clean beat and raise (revenue growth resumed, NCO rate lowest in years, ROE inside target range, EPS guide raised, interest expense down), but the +31% move already prices most of it; some drift potential from a thinly covered name, with a 15% corporate debt refinancing option and risk-based pricing tests still unreflected.

Large Core FFO miss and guidance cut, NAV cut, a Q4 dividend shortfall with a likely cut, and unhedged floating-rate debt (about $0.14 per share per 25bp) were met with only a -2.8% move; October occupancy is still weak, though the buyback and asset-sale plans limit the downside.

Trio production guidance raised, 2026 Trio output guided to 320-330k tons, about 30% IRR growth capex, buybacks stepped up, and the stock trades near 3.5x EBITDA with a net cash balance sheet, but the +0.9% move reflects little of this; offset by a Q3 Moab production delay and Wendover lithium timing slippage.

Guidance cut (EBITDA midpoint about $56M to $50M, about $20M of data center revenue slipping into early next year, Q4 margin the trough) is offset by a pipeline above $200M and a clear margin-recovery path, and the +1.5% price move already reflects both.
A beat, a conservative Q4 guide, new buybacks and a stated 25%+ FCF yield support modest drift after the +41.6% move, but most of the news is likely already priced in.

Record FCF, a logistics margin target hit early, clinical share gains and a new $20M buyback support some post-earnings drift, but the +22% move already prices most of this and Q4 logistics is guided flat with weak October industry volumes.

De-REIT news (about +11% GAAP book value from the DTA, NOL tax savings, a preferred-for-common exchange at a premium acting like a buyback) looks under-reflected in a +0.6% move, but the dividend cut to $0.02, a Q3 GAAP loss, weak Aspire results, and likely income-holder turnover offset most of it.

Solid quarter (FFO/AFFO up, G&A cut, occupancy 90.1%, 9-10% acquisition yields) but the +9.9% move already reflects it, and the unresolved geriatric behavioral tenant sale and delayed acquisitions offset it.
